title: Rules 30 and 45 are expected to be universal

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rules 30 and 45 are expected to be universal

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although the localized structures found in rules 30 and 45 on repetitive backgrounds all move at the same speed and so cannot interact, preventing a rule 110-style proof, rules 30 and 45 will nevertheless turn out to be universal.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So although this means that the particular type of approach we used to demonstrate the universality of rule 110 cannot immediately be used for rule 30 or rule 45, it certainly does not mean that these rules are not in the end universal.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “The Threshold of Universality in Cellular Automata” (from p. 694), p. 701. Scope: the rule 30 and rule 45 elementary cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-24: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is precise enough once universality is standardly defined, but public simulations do not settle it. New mathematical constructions or impossibility results are required.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct a computable encoding and simulation of a known universal machine in each of rules 30 and 45, or prove an invariant that makes such simulation impossible. Simulations can search for components but cannot by themselves establish universality.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No accepted universality proof is available for these rules.

Universality cannot be confirmed by bounded runs.

Class-3 information spreading obstructs known construction methods.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both rules are fully specified, so universality is a sharp mathematical property, and pieces of evidence such as one-step emulation can be recomputed. No proof that either rule is universal or that either is not is available as a finished, checkable argument. Those partial experiments are exactly the ones the book says do not settle the prediction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Universality means a computable encoding under which rule 30, and likewise rule 45, emulates every Turing machine. A published encoding would confirm each rule; a proof that some Turing computation is impossible in that rule would refute it. Equal-speed gliders on periodic backgrounds can be searched separately and do not decide the question.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A finite search cannot exhaust encodings, and non-universality of these rules is not known to be finitely checkable.

The natural glider proof used for rule 110 does not apply if every localized structure has the same velocity, but that does not decide universality.
